Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Jeff Stelling has revealed that producers would unplug televisions and hide remotes during filming of Celebrity Race Across the World, which left the veteran sports broadcaster completely cut off from football and his beloved Hartlepool United.

Stelling is taking part in the latest series of the hit adventure travel show, teaming with his son Matt in a 4,660-mile race from the Malaysian city of Kuching to the finish line in Melbourne, Australia on a budget of £26 a day.

The former Soccer Saturday presenter, who ended over 30 years of service with Sky Sports in May 2023, is a passionate lifelong Hartlepool fan and serves as honorary president of the National League club.

But as he traversed the depths of South East Asia with no phone and limited technology, he was left completely in the dark about the club’s performance at the tail-end of the 2025/26 season.

“We couldn’t get any football scores at all because we’ve got no way [of finding them out],” Stelling told The Independent.

Industry observers note that “If you’re within your checkpoints, if there’s a TV in your room, they [the producers] make sure it’s either disconnected or else they don’t give you a remote, so they make sure that that’s taken away. You’ve got no contact.”.

The fourth series of the show, which aired its first episode on Wednesday, was filmed from February to April earlier this year.

During that time, Hartlepool experienced a mixed bag of results - going on their joint-best win streak of the season with three consecutive victories, only for that run to be ended by their heaviest defeat of the season: a 7-0 hammering at Wealdstone at the end of March.

Stelling notes he was out of the loop for all of this, however, which allowed him to let his dreams run wild as the National League season approached its climax.

Recent findings suggest that “For me, it meant I could fantasise that we were winning every game,” he added. “And then when we finished, I found out the truth that we hadn’t been winning every game.”.

Hartlepool ended last season in ninth, 12 points adrift of the National League play-off places.

His agony without any knowledge of the Pools’ performance was not a shared experience with his youngest son, though, with Matt a Brighton supporter.

“Well obviously, my relationship with this son’s a bit stressed because he’s a Brighton fan!” Stelling joked, whose older son meanwhile follows his father’s lead in supporting Hartlepool.

“No, we’ve always gotten on really well,” he continued, “but it’s sort of challenging for both of us, but probably more for him, that you are going to spend six weeks, 24 hours a day, with your dad - often sharing a bed or sharing the same floor.

“Different generations have got different views of things, so inevitably, over that period of time, in the sort of intense situation that you’re in, there are inevitably going to be occasions when you’ve got to bite your tongue, on both sides.

In a recent development, “But it was brilliant. As I say, we were close before. We’re probably even closer afterwards.”.

Thomas Sorensen attributes 'a bit of a bust-up' with then-manager Martin O'Neill as the reason his spell at Aston Villa came to an end, 20 years ago.

The stopper was a reliable presence between the sticks for Aston Villa from 2003 to 2007, only to find himself out of favour throughout 2007/08.

Sorensen admits it was the most difficult time of his career, but he found a new lease of life after making the move to newly-promoted Stoke City the following season.

Recent findings suggest that sorensen told FourFourTwo: "We had a bit of a bust-up. I got injured in pre-season and they brought Scott Carson in from Liverpool.

"I was contacted by the Danish press and said I couldn’t quite understand that situation: ‘Why would he come in if he wasn’t going to play?’.

Recent findings suggest that "It wasn’t ill-intended by me, but I don’t know if that upset Martin. He’s definitely not on my Christmas card list.

"I just worked my socks off for other opportunities and luckily that came at Stoke.".

Sorensen admits that he had his doubts about that move, saying: "It was a bit of a gamble, but it reminded me of going back to my Sunderland days.

It has been revealed that "Tony Pulis was very old school and they had that team spirit. I felt at home in that environment and I loved the challenge.

"It was an opportunity to show people that there was still life in the old dog. It obviously went a lot better than we thought. I signed for one year and seven years later I was still there.

"It was us against the world. Everyone hated us because of the way we played – the physicality and the long throws.

"Having that unity made it even better. We had some great seasons there. Pulis was really good at pitting us against everyone else, like Match of the Day, because we were last on and everyone was talking badly about the way we played.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For those hoping for reunion between Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson, the odds are finally in your favor.

In a recent development, the original Hunger Games stars walked the red carpet together for the first time in 11 years, attending the New York City premiere of the franchise's new Sunrise on the Reaping prequel on Nov. 16.

Industry observers note that jennifer, 36, seemed to channel series villain President Snow with her long black Christian Dior coat, as it featured a white fur collar and rose embroidery on the train, which she paired with matching open-toe heels. Meanwhile, Josh, 34, let the games begin in an all-black suit with leather boots.

Industry observers note that but they weren't the only familiar faces to leave the crowd totally star-crossed. After all, their former castmates Woody Harrelson, Elizabeth Banks, Jena Malone, Willow Shields and Amandla Stenberg were also in attendance, posing for an epic group photo with their longtime director Francis Lawrence and The Hunger Games author Suzanne Collins.

Jennifer and Josh reprised their respective roles of Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark in Sunrise on the Reaping, a prequel starring Mckenna Grace and Joseph Zada that follows Hamish Abernathy (played by Woody in the OG series) during his time competing in 50th Hunger Games before becoming a mentor.

And for Jennifer, it was a capitol idea to return to the franchise.

Sources indicate that "Oh man, it was unbelievable," the Oscar winner raved in an October episode of the Call Her Daddy podcast. "It was so crazy because it was the same crew. It was the same camera guys, the same [assistant director] who I've worked with a million times too, 'cause I love him.".

In fact, she and Josh "didn't walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other.".

"It was so emotional," Jennifer added. "It was so beautiful.".

While this will be the first time the actress and Josh share a screen together since 2015's The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2, the two have remained close through the years. As Josh previously pointed out, Jennifer even texted him when their respective movies Five Nights at Freddy's and No Hard Feelings were released around the same time in 2023.

It has been revealed that "She was like, 'My movie's  No. 1 on Netflix, and your's is  No. 1 at the box office! Let's go!'" the actor recalled in a 2024 interview with Variety. "I was like, 'I love you!'".

So, as the pair volunteer as tributes for a Hunger Games reunion, read on for more behind-the-scenes secrets about the franchise.

Recent findings suggest that 1. When we tell you every young actress volunteered as tribute to play The Hunger Games' bow-and-arrow wielding heroine Katniss Everdeen, we really mean it. Hailee Steinfeld, Abigail Breslin, Emma Roberts, Saoirse Ronan, Chloë Grace Moretz, Jodelle Ferland, Lyndsy Fonseca, Emily Browning, Shailene Woodley, Kaya Scodelario and Troian Bellisario all auditioned, but Oscar nominee Jennifer Lawrence was director Gary Ross' first choice from the beginning.

Industry observers note that "I absolutely cast the right person for the role and in my view there wasn't even a question who the best Katniss was," Ross told Entertainment Weekly in 2011. "It was the easiest casting decision I ever made in my life.".

According to recent reports, 2. But Lawrence needed time to decide whether or not she wanted to take on the role, nervous about the level of fame she would be catapulted into. (See: Twilight's Kristen Stewart and Robert Pattinson.).

It has been revealed that "It was the middle of the night in England, and I was in bed when I got the call," Lawrence told MTV News. "And I was so in love with the books and the script, and suddenly it was right in my face—and the size of the decision was terrifying." Ultimately, it was her mom, Karen Lawrence, who helped her commit to the movie.

"She called me a hypocrite, because when I was doing indie movies and everyone was asking why I didn't do studio movies, I remarked, 'The size of the movie doesn't matter,'" Lawrence recalled. "And she said, 'Here's a movie you love and you were thinking of turning it down because of its size.' I thought, 'I don't want to miss out because I'm scared. Me being scared, I never want that to stop me from doing something.' But I knew in my heart that I wanted it—it was about working out all the fears.".

3. After Lawrence was officially announced as Katniss, the Internet did what it tends to do: Get mad that the 20-year-old actress was older than the character, who is 16 in the first book, and that she was (gasp!) blonde. But Ross wasn't concerned with the initial backlash, telling Entertainment Weekly that The Hunger Games author Suzanne Collins, who co-wrote the script, signed off on Lawrence's casting.

"Not only did Suzanne not have an issue with Jen's age, she felt you need someone of a certain maturity and power to be Katniss," the filmmaker noted. "This is a girl who needs to incite a revolution. We can't have an insubstantial person play her, and we can't have someone who's too young to play this. Suzanne was incredibly adamant about this. Far from being too old, she was very concerned that we would cast someone who was too young.".

Industry observers note that 4. Lawrence paid no attention to the response to her casting, telling MTV News, "No, because the internet to me is like a black hole. I never really go on it.".

In a recent development, she added, "I wasn't really aware that everybody was so upset until after I got my hair dyed. Then people were like, 'Oh my gosh, blonde hair can turn brown!'".

It has been revealed that 5. Lawrence was paid just $500,000 for the first movie. For the sequel, 2013's Catching Fire, she netted $10 million.

In a recent development, 6. When it came to Katniss' fellow District 12 tribute and eventual love interest Peeta Mellark, Alexander Ludwig, Hunter Parrish, Lucas Till and Evan Peters read for the part, which ultimately went to Josh Hutcherson.

Recent findings suggest that "When I read the book, I thought Peeta would be the hardest role to cast, and I feel so lucky that we found someone who embodies every aspect of such a complex character,"  Ross said in a statement at the time. "I can't wait to work with Josh.".

In a recent development, 7. For Gale Hawthorne, Katniss' brooding childhood best friend, Liam Hemsworth beat out David Henrie, Drew Roy and Robbie Amell. "Gale is a young man who uses words very sparingly, so the onus was on the actor we cast to capture him by showing, not telling," producer Nina Jacobson noted. "This was accomplished so beautifully in Suzanne's writing, and Liam was able to translate it so naturally to the screen.".

In a recent development, 8. All three leads had to dye their hair for the movie, with the naturally blonde Hemsworth going dark, Hutcherson bleaching his locks and Lawrence going brunette after an extensive process to find the right brunette shade.

Hair designer and head stylist Linda Flowers revealed to Cosmopolitan in 2014 that they rented six $5,000 wigs in a range of brown colors, with Ross ultimately picking the darkest hue to use as a guide when dyeing Lawrence's hair even though his star preferred the lightest.

9. To prepare for the physically demanding role, Lawrence underwent various workout methods.

"It's lots of training but the training's actually really fun," she told MTV News. "I've done archery for about six weeks, and rock climbing, tree climbing, combat, running and vaulting. But also yoga and things like that, to stay catlike.".

10. Lawrence had an accident on the last day of her six-week training program, hitting a wall during an exercise that almost delayed production.

"I ran at it and my foot didn't go up, so I caught the wall with my stomach," Lawrence revealed to The Hollywood Reporter. "My trainer thought I had burst my spleen. I had to get a CAT scan and go into a tube where they put this fiery liquid in your body." Fortunately, nothing was broken and a bruised Lawrence was able to continue.

It has been revealed that 11. Hutcherson also trained extensively prior to filming, telling Collider in 2012, "I'd never really done that for a movie. I put on about 15 pounds of muscle, so that was a lot of eating chicken, and a very high protein, low carb diet.".

12. As for Hemsworth, he revealed his older brother, Thor's Chris Hemsworth, offered him some surprising advice to prep for the movie.

In a recent development, "My brother texted me before shooting and told me to lose weight," Hemsworth revealed to The Hollywood Reporter. "He remarked, 'It's called The Hunger Games, not The Eating Games!'".

13. Several weeks into filming, Lawrence knocked Hutcherson unconscious when she accidentally kicked him in the head.

"She was being a real show-off, thinking that she was Jackie Chan or something," Hutcherson recalled in an interview with Yahoo. "[She was] throwing these air kicks and was like, ‘Josh, I can kick over your head!' And then crack! She clipped me in the temple…I don't really remember, because I got knocked out." When Hutcherson came to again, he said, "She was crying. She felt terrible. I woke up with her [crying], laying over me.".

Recent findings suggest that 14. While filming in North Carolina, the cast and crew faced 100-degree heat, daily rain showers and bears that would wander onto set when they smelled food.

15. Woody Harrelson initially passed twice on the role of Katniss and Peeta's drunken mentor Haymitch Abernathy, admitting to The Hollywood Reporter in 2017, "I didn't have any idea it would be that big, but I didn't think it was a good part. I was wrong. It was a terrific part and it was a terrific thing, but thank God Gary Ross called me.".

It has been revealed that 16. Elizabeth Banks required daily manicures for her look as Katniss and Peeta's Capitol escort Effie Trinket and the intricate nails proved to be quite impractical on-set.

In a recent development, "I literally didn't function," Banks told Collider in 2012. "I had ladies-in-waiting that did everything for me. I couldn't type on my phone. I couldn't go to the bathroom. I couldn't get in and out of [my costume]. By the time I got to the lunch line, everybody was back in their trailers, done with lunch. I was like, 'There's no one to eat with! I just got here!' It took me 25 minutes to get in and out of my costume.".

Sources indicate that 17. Lenny Kravitz, who was cast as Katniss' stylist and confidant Cinna, actually had a relationship with Lawrence prior to filming, thanks to his daughter Zoe Kravitz.

"They were doing X-Men: First Class here in London, I live in Paris so they'd take the train and my house was basically the flop house for the cast," he told HeyUGuys in 2012. "So I would bring different people for the weekend to hang out in Paris, so I met Jennifer and immediately just fell in love with her. She's just amazing. Super funny, really funny, at all times she keeps you cracking up. So I got to know her like that. It was quite funny when I asked Gary 'So who's playing Katniss?' and he said 'Jennifer Lawrence,' and he liked the fact that we already had a relationship. He thought that'd help because I already kind of look at her like a daughter in a way, so it's going to be good.".

Industry observers note that 18. "Safe & Sound," the film's original song co-written and performed by Taylor Swift featuring the Civil Wars, won Best Song Written for Visual Media at the 55th Annual Grammy Awards in 2013.

It has been revealed that 19. When the film was released in March 2012, it set records for opening day (grossing $67.3 million) and opening weekend for a non-sequel ($152 million). It went on to become the third highest grossing movie of the year.

According to recent reports, 20. While he was initially set to return, director Ross ultimately stepped away from the franchise, with Francis Lawrence directing the three followup films.

Sources indicate that "Well, it was a very hard decision," Ross explained to Variety in March 2022. "I think what people didn't realize is that I had two jobs. I wrote and I directed, and you do one of those things before you do the other. There was honestly no time to do both well in the three-and-a half months between movies, so I moved on. I got to make Free State of Jones, which not many people saw but remains one of my favorite pieces of work, so—all good.".

Swansea in fight to keep Matos amid Strasbourg interest

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vitor Matos spent five years on Jurgen Klopp's staff at Liverpool.
  • Vitor Matos is close to leaving Swansea City to take charge of French top-flight club Strasbourg.
  • Strasbourg have made an official approach for the Swansea head coach, who looks likely to depart even though there is no agreement yet between the clubs over a compensation package.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vitor Matos spent five years on Jurgen Klopp's staff at Liverpool.

Vitor Matos is close to leaving Swansea City to take charge of French top-flight club Strasbourg.

Strasbourg have made an official approach for the Swansea head coach, who looks likely to depart even though there is no agreement yet between the clubs over a compensation package.

Matos was at Swansea's training ground on Tuesday morning, but is understood to have told the Championship side he wants to leave.

Matos is under contract until 2030, meaning Swansea will be due significant compensation should he depart.

But that has not stopped Strasbourg targeting the 38-year-old Portuguese, who had been due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea later this month.

Current Strasbourg boss Hugo Oliveira, Matos' fellow countryman, is under pressure after a run of five defeats in six matches.

Oliveira has managed only three wins in 10 league games since succeeding Gary O'Neil - who left to take over at Ipswich Town â in July.

O'Neil led Strasbourg to an eighth-place finish last season, but they are currently 13th in Ligue 1, only two points above the relegation zone.

Strasbourg are a sister club of Premier League side Chelsea.

Matos has turned Swansea from potential relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls since taking charge, with the club 20th in the Championship when he took over last November.

The Swans finished 11th last season and have made further strides in the first third of this campaign.

Vitor Matos led Swansea to seven wins in their first 10 league games of the season, though they have since lost four in five.

Matos' team have been among the early-season pacesetters in the second tier, enjoying two spells on top of the table, but their form has dipped in recent weeks.

Swansea have suffered four defeats in their past five matches, though they remain only three points off top spot going into Saturday's home game against West Bromwich Albion.

Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he has also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact at Swansea.

When asked in October about the Palace links, Matos said: "I'm Swansea manager. I love being here, love my players, love the staff, so my focus is always on the next game and what we can do better.".

In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs, though he played down the idea of the former Liverpool coach having his head turned.

"The reality is there'll always be interest in anyone performing well in any role on and off the pitch," Gorringe said.

"That's one of the outcomes of being successful - we're aware of that.

"[But] we're all quite happy. We've all agreed to go on this journey together and we hope that Vitor is here a long time.".

After West Brom visit, Swansea go to second-placed Middlesbrough next Tuesday before Cardiff City make the short trip west for the first south Wales derby in two seasons on Sunday, 29 November.

Should Matos depart, it is thought likely that a number of his backroom team will also move on.

Vitor Matos latest: Strasbourg close in on Swansea head coach.

Vitor Matos is relatively inexperienced, if you look at his senior management experience alone, but his wealth of footballing experience is evident when taking a wider look at his footballing journey.

Speaking to BBC Sport earlier this season, Matos explained how his 23 years in football have informed his development - a journey that began when a 15-year-old Matos was inspired by Jose Mourinho's Champions League triumph with Porto.

So, although he only took his first managerial job at the start of last season in the second division of Portugal, to call Matos an overnight success story would be false.

He developed an understanding of positional play while working as a youth coach at FC Porto, before moving to China. As technical director and an under-16 coach of Shandong Taishan, he added layers of knowledge to his positional game:.

"In China, I understood that to arrive at a more positional game, you could have different steps beforehand," he explained.

"There is a benefit to having more players close to each other, rather than spreading them over space.

"If you spread them over space, you are demanding that, technically, they can solve many situations one-v-one. If they come closer to the ball, you can generate more possibilities. You can create a tempo that allows other players to be better in the massive spaces.".

The uniqueness of these overloads, around the ball, have been a hallmark of some of Swansea's impressive attacking play this season.

Following stints in Portugal and China, he then found himself working alongside Jurgen Klopp and Pep Lijnders at Liverpool, which provided him a greater understanding of senior football at the elite level.

"Liverpool influenced me a lot in terms of counter-pressing, pressing, intensity, and what makes you grow as a team," he said.

"The most important thing is how much you believe in your idea, and this style is how I see football. That's why I want this to be the foundation for our team.".

Tech Report: As El Niño builds, studies of extreme marine heatwaves must start now

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that coral nurseries, such as this one in French Polynesia, can be used to study the resilience of the organisms in real-world settings.
  • According to recent reports, with temperatures in the Pacific Ocean at record-high levels and forecasts of an extreme El Niño climate event, intense marine heatwaves are expected around the world in the coming year1,2.
  • The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that coral nurseries, such as this one in French Polynesia, can be used to study the resilience of the organisms in real-world settings. Credit: Alexis Rosenfeld/Getty.

According to recent reports, with temperatures in the Pacific Ocean at record-high levels and forecasts of an extreme El Niño climate event, intense marine heatwaves are expected around the world in the coming year1,2. Scientists must prepare to study these extreme conditions now, so that managers of marine resources and decision makers can develop and implement response strategies and communities can proposal for a hotter future.

The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?

The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?

Recent findings suggest that el Niño is part of a recurring natural cycle in Earth’s climate in which warmer waters in the central and eastern Pacific alter ocean and atmospheric circulation, affecting weather worldwide. Marine heatwaves associated with El Niño provide opportunities to study ecosystems under real-world stress conditions and on scales that cannot be replicated in a laboratory.

According to recent reports, marine heatwaves can be forecast weeks or months ahead, giving researchers time to design field studies, deploy instruments and collect baseline data. Investigations can be designed to test theories and improve our understanding of ecological processes, thresholds and recovery mechanisms in a rapidly warming ocean.

It has been revealed that such knowledge can inform decisions about how to manage marine resources, such as whether to close fisheries. Much has been learnt about marine heatwaves since the last El Niño, in 2023–24 (see ‘Hot water’). But these lessons need to be consolidated and scaled up into consistent, long-term preparedness plans.

Source: Climate Reanalyzer (CC-BY-4.0); go.nature.com/4zae69a.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, effective approaches established in one place can be extended to others. Australia is a leader in developing early-warning systems and response prepares for adaptation to a more extreme ocean climate. Other nations (including the United Kingdom, the United States, Latest Zealand and Peru) have improved their awareness of these events and put in place observation systems, forecasts and briefings, policy mechanisms and (in a few cases) adaptation measures.

According to recent reports, but further action is needed, particularly in locations that have previously been unaffected by severe marine heatwaves. Here, we highlight seven priorities in increasing marine heatwave preparedness.

Seasonal forecasts with lead times of several months are now being delivered in various regions, including the United States3 and Australia4, and such systems are being developed in the United Kingdom and Fresh Zealand5 and for the Mediterranean Sea6.

Forecasting relies on physical and statistical models to predict probable ocean temperatures7. Data from sustained surface and below-surface observations are essential for initializing models and verifying predictions, building users’ confidence in forecasts.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

It has been revealed that but managers want to know more precisely what the duration and intensity of a marine heatwave is expected to be. Forecasts become less accurate the further ahead they look and at fine spatial scales, such as along coasts. Improved ocean monitoring, a better understanding of the drivers of marine heatwaves and continued refinements of model physics are needed to improve forecast accuracy7.

Advances in machine learning are expected to be transformative. Next-generation models that incorporate ocean physics might be able to predict unprecedented marine heatwaves more accurately than current technologies can. Downscaling global climate models to inshore regions using machine-learning techniques could also increase the usefulness of forecasts in places where most marine-resource consumers operate.

According to recent reports, planning for and communication about impending marine heatwaves are also improving1. In 2023, engagement was piecemeal and often only in response to events that were already in progress. Activities are now more proactive and structured.

It has been revealed that coordinated briefings that translate forecasts into action provide ways of engaging with affected groups and planning ahead. Such communication strategies should be implemented around the world4,8. National briefings provide a broad overview of marine heatwave risks and impacts. Regional and industry specialists can provide further local advice.

Industry observers note that for example, Australia’s national marine climate briefing series4 has been running since 2023. Similar meetings (led or contributed to by some of us) have taken place for the western Pacific Ocean (G.S.) and in the United Kingdom (C.R.), Brazil (K.E.S.), Singapore (C.M.S.) and Latest Zealand (C.M.S.).

Seafood-producing firms and conservation managers need a menu of actions to choose from when a marine heatwave looms. Options include adjusting collection strategies, temporarily closing fisheries and modifying aquaculture operations1.

Recent findings suggest that australia has developed regional and industry-specific response intends for marine heatwaves8. Response teams for fisheries are active during warming events and provide coordinated mechanisms for assessment, communication and management actions4,9.

Impacts of marine heatwaves are being monitored in restored giant kelp forests in Tasmania, Australia.Credit: Scott Ling/University of Tasmania.

Early-warning systems and interagency coordination are key components of timely responses. Industry has also adopted operating protocols to reduce the impacts of marine heatwaves on animal health and food-product quality. For example, abalone fisheries in Latest South Wales have changed how sea snails (Haliotis spp.) are fished, handled and prepared for live export10. Other regions could benefit from similar plans4.

Recent findings suggest that for example, fishing of Peruvian anchoveta (Engraulis ringens), the source of around 20% of fishmeal and fish oil globally, has already been curbed by the current El Niño. In 2023, the fishery had to be closed, resulting in an estimated loss11 of US$1.4 billion. This year, an alert in February prompted Peruvian authorities to bring the fishing season forwards by two weeks and reduce the total allowable catch of anchoveta and white anchovy (Anchoa nasus) by more than 30% to 1.9 million tonnes. This meant that fisheries could catch about 450,000 tonnes before the heatwave intensified and the season was ended in May.

In 2023, marine heatwave preparedness was recognized as inadequate in most regions. The emphasis then was mainly on raising risk awareness in sectors such as fisheries and aquaculture1. However, these and other industries need to adapt to a changing ocean, too.

Awareness has now grown among sectors and institutions, and behaviours have begun to change. For example, Australian marine climate briefings draw engagement from aquaculture and fishery managers, marine tourism operators, policymakers, researchers and individual fishers4.

In the United States, forecasts of marine heatwaves trigger advice to fishers regarding increases in interactions with marine mammals as the overlap between animals’ hunting grounds and deployed fishing gear expands, which can result in fishery closures. Coral-reef managers involved in restoration efforts can scale back replanting efforts and start collecting genetic material.

The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare.

The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare.

In the Mediterranean Sea, limiting diving tourism at coral reefs to minimize damage during marine heatwaves has been proposed, mirroring practices that were adopted in Asia during the 2023–24 marine heatwaves11.

Sources indicate that in the Cook Islands’ black-pearl industry, seasonal forecasts have been proposed for supporting decisions around adaptive management aimed at reducing the thermal stress of oysters. These include increased reliance on hatchery production under controlled temperature conditions and preferential harvesting of pearls during cooler periods of the year.

In the United Kingdom, a national marine heatwave network and code of best practice have been established, enabling the exchange of transdisciplinary knowledge. Similar transfers of experience, capacity and lessons learnt between jurisdictions can accelerate preparedness globally and help to embed risk management into routine decision-making processes4.

Industry observers note that the 2023 El Niño led to calls to strengthen monitoring and research capacity to improve the detection of, understanding of and response to marine heatwaves. Observation networks are now becoming a core component of preparedness and response plans, providing the information needed to support forecasting, impact assessment, management interventions and long-term adaptation strategies12.

Sources indicate that targeted uses of gliders and intensified monitoring strategies can bolster research, situational awareness and management decisions12. Research has expanded into understanding ecological resilience and adaptation. For example, genetic studies are identifying traits that might enhance the capacity of key fishery or habitat-forming species13 to persist under increasing thermal stress.

Researchers in Florida are studying corals obtained from local reefs as part of restoration efforts.Credit: Chandan Khanna/AFP via Getty.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past.
  • Sources indicate that so when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America.

In a recent development, outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike.

Sources indicate that so when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson.

“You know what I noticed?” Pochettino asked, smiling as he recounted the story during a meeting with reporters on Monday. “[Guardiola had a] good relationship with JT.”.

Back then, Pochettino didn’t seem to be going anywhere. Only a month earlier, he’d signed a four-year contract to guide the US through the 2030 World Cup. Guardiola was, and still is, in the middle of a year-long sabbatical from coaching. He remains the federation’s white whale, often mentioned in the same breath as the US job over the past decade-plus but just as swiftly dismissed as a pipe dream.

Just three months after taking in that game at Yankee Stadium, Pochettino is on his way to Manchester United and Guardiola has once again found himself at the center of the rumor mill, with reports suggesting that he and US Soccer are set for exploratory talks.

On Monday, Pochettino was asked what he’d tell the Barcelona and Manchester City legend if he was asked for his opinion on the US job.

It has been revealed that “Take it,” Pochettino stated, flatly. “Why? Because it’s a perfect moment to arrive at the federation. Everything is on the right path, in the right direction. Of course, take it. Of course, you are going to find really good players, good people – the players can fit his style.”.

According to recent reports, guardiola was one of many topics the Argentinian manager covered during the roundtable, which lasted about an hour. At times defiant, at times emotional and cycling through Spanish and English, Pochettino spoke of his potential legacy at US Soccer, what lies ahead for him at United and how he views soccer in America as a whole.

Quotes have been lightly edited and condensed for clarity.

However you assess his results, one of the inarguable successes of the Pochettino era are the relatively unheralded players whose status has risen over his tenure. The Argentine cited defender Alex Freeman and midfielder Sebastian Berhalter as two such examples, both of whom were playing in MLS when making their national team debuts under Pochettino and both now playing in Europe. Asked how he assesses players to add to the national team, and how he compares players across different leagues and playing styles, Pochettino insisted that the level of competition matters less than individual form.

Recent findings suggest that “You need to project the individual player,” Pochettino noted. “Because he’s playing well, the level is no concern. That player can be good, like Freeman, like Sebastian. That is the example, and I think that is so important. There is talent everywhere … This one is one of the things that we learn – all [of us], we were young and then we start to be a coach, no? That we cannot make a mistake [and] measure the level of the player because of the level of the league.”.

With the US being his first international job, there were some doubts going in about how Pochettino would adapt to coaching without daily contact with his players and staff.

“I am ready [to return]. This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here,” Pochettino said. “Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’ [He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool]. But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good. But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”.

But what did Pochettino think of his maiden international job?

Industry observers note that “I like and not like,” he noted. “I like because it provides you the possibility to manage your time, to be busy, but at the same time, be free and to have some time with your family. Now, I have a grandchild, and [number] two is coming. You can share the life with your people. But now, ciao, because now is [gestures] tra-tra-tra-tra-tra. It’s impossible to spend time with the people you want.”.

According to recent reports, in the grand scheme of international football, the US national team coaching job has never been close to the top of the list of most desirable destinations. Pochettino’s hire was seen as a possible sign that could be changing. Now, after nearly two years in the position, Pochettino believes it has.

Sources indicate that “The vision from Europe, I promise it is completely different after the World Cup,” Pochettino said. “Now, being head coach of the USA is more prestigious. If Manchester United, or Real Madrid, or Barcelona is coming for the US coach, if you start to think about that, if you are another coach – maybe [Antonio] Conte, someone else, you say ‘oh, this is a great opportunity.’ [In my case], ‘Oh, Pochettino, from Chelsea he goes to the US? And now to Manchester United.’.

Pochettino has coached some of the most famous players and clubs in the world, giving him a unique perspective on how soccer has developed in the US. Pochettino stopped short of prescribing neat solutions to improve the sport, though.

Recent findings suggest that “I think that business [and] the sport, is [done] in a holistic way. Everything is crucial, and you cannot pick one. You cannot change one [thing], and that can change everything,” he mentioned. “I think it’s a little bit of everything that you need to change. If you adjust this, you need to adjust this. The balance of the thing changes if you touch here, that will force you to touch all the areas in soccer here, or in the world To find the good balance, no? A process of little by little, is all that we made in these last two years. I think it’s the beginning of [a process]. If that has continuity, it’s the beginning of the fresh soccer in the USA that can be.

Industry observers note that “I think that is, for me, the beginning of the change for the future: that idea that the American player can be very good, can be very competitive. The talent is here; it’s so powerful in this country. I think that is why I feel proud. Maybe that was our job, because I don’t believe in coincidence. That has happened because something needed to happen. Now the tough job is done. Maybe now [the United job] is my reward because of this tough job.”.

Tech Report: 'Warhammer Survivors' is the perfect gateway into the 40K universe

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd.
  • In a recent development, developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this upcoming spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe.
  • When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd. Warhammer Survivors changes that, finally providing curious gamers with an easy entry point into the grim darkness of the 41st millennium.

In a recent development, developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this upcoming spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe. This means heroes and enemies from all over the Warhammer mythos meet together in a bite-sized game that anyone can figure out and enjoy in less than five minutes.

When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into.

According to recent reports, warhammer Survivors isn't bogged down by dense lore, involved mechanics, or massive campaign playthroughs. It's more of an "inspired by" effort that gives casuals a small taste of the series' iconic characters — including Boltgun's Malum Caedo — and factions like the terrifying Tyranids, the raucous Orks, and the foul forces of Chaos.

All of 40K's (and Age of Sigmar's) recognizable elements are on display, but they serve more as flavoring sprinkled on top of Vampire Survivors' successful formula.

If you're new to the Survivors-like subgenre, it's a unique gaming experience. You battle an endless onslaught of enemies that slowly march towards you, with your character passively attacking automatically. You only need to move them around sprawling arenas and select level-up upgrades and items after collecting enough gems (skulls in this case).

The moment-to-moment gameplay is as simple as it can get outside of walking sims and interactive "experiences," but there's a deceiving depth to item synergies and how to correctly "build" characters to endure all the carnage.

Unlike Poncle's original game, Warhammer Survivors struggles a bit to get going. The early hours are sluggish until you unlock certain meta upgrades, but its still got that Vampire Survivors magic at its core.

As far as "podcast/gym games" go, this is a perfect fit. There's just enough going on to keep one's brain engaged, but minimal inputs and a tight overarching design lead to a rhythm that's easy to get into without using much brainpower. It's oddly satisfying to weave through enemies and level up your firepower, watching a single Astra Militarum grunt grow into a full Lasgun-spamming, chainsword-wielding wrecking ball.

Sources indicate that achievement and unlock hunters will find enough to bite into here, too. It's unclear if the devs will continue to add more Warhammer 40K and Age of Sigmar deep cuts to this game via DLCs and free updates, but those universes have daunting depths to explore. This really could become a gateway game for future 40K fans: by the time they realize they're hooked, they'll already have 2000 pts of space marines painted and ready to play.

Sources indicate that as massive sci-fi and fantasy properties try to aggressively expand and absorb more and more fans, it's easy to pander to already-converted diehards too much. And sure, we can't wait for strategy heavyweights like Dawn of War 4 and Total War: WH40K either, but they're hardly good recommendations for folks who don't even know what a Space Marine is or why the robotic Necrons are so grumpy.

Industry observers note that warhammer Survivors won't answer those questions beyond the surface-level iconography, but it's fun enough to push those curious to dig deeper and embrace the same material in more mature video game genres... and maybe even pick up a few miniatures.

Warhammer Survivors is now available on PC (Steam & GOG), PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 1/2, and mobile (iOS & Android). It's also playable on Game Pass.

Fran Ruiz is our resident Star Wars guy. His hunger for movies and TV series is only matched by his love for video games. On top of writing features and other longform articles for Space.com since 2021, he is a frequent collaborator of VG247 and other gaming sites. He also serves as associate editor over at Star Wars News Net and its sister site, Movie News Net.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career.
  • Andy Robertson has become Scotland's most capped men's international after starting in Monday's Nations League defeat in Switzerland to reach 103 appearances for his country.
  • Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he surpassed his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul had stood for 40 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career.

Andy Robertson has become Scotland's most capped men's international after starting in Monday's Nations League defeat in Switzerland to reach 103 appearances for his country.

Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he surpassed his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul had stood for 40 years.

After moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham Hotspur left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare.

But, in St Gallen, the spotlight shone on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he moves solo at the summit, even if the scoreline was a disappointment.

Robertson set to make history, but hero Dalglish will always be King.

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson.

Andy Robertson on his hero, Kenny Dalglish.

For much of this year, Dalglish was the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.

'King Kenny' topped the list on 102 caps - earning his last in November 1986 against Luxembourg when in a player-manager role at Liverpool.

Few since have even come close to toppling him - and Robertson is keen to stress the throne is still reserved for Dalglish - but it is perhaps fitting it is the current captain, given their great friendship.

Which allows Dalglish to say he's not having any of it.

According to recent reports, "He always says: 'You've got millions more games. Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.

"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.

In a recent development, "It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up.".

Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.

But not out of John McGinn's - the midfielder's double against North Macedonia on Friday took him to within six of the legendary duo.

The Aston Villa captain is lurking only eight caps behind Robertson on the all-time caps list, too, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.

Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 33 times more than any other player.

At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.

Now he is the only man to have led Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.

Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.

Industry observers note that "Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant.".

One of those young players is 20-year-old Findlay Curtis, who told the media the night before Robertson's historic night that his captain has "probably been the biggest role model" he's looked up to since joining the international set-up earlier this year.

Perhaps that was because Robertson did him a turn back in the day. Unbeknownst to the skipper.

Rangers winger Curtis was only 14 during the Covid pandemic and was partial to playing a bit of Fifa, and Robertson was a star in his team.

In a recent development, "I was just thinking, I had him in my Fifa team," he explained. "[For] defending and he was just fast as well.

"What a servant he has been for the country.".

'I had him in my Fifa team!' - Findlay Curtis on going from fan to team-mate of Robertson.

Robertson has played under four permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.

It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.

McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played five times for fresh boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.

However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair led Scotland to three major tournaments.

Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.

"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke noted at the World Cup.

"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad.".

Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.

Industry observers note that crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.

Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.

According to recent reports, he has started 101 of his 103 caps, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.

The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with?

At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.

Andorra owner Gerard Pique believes that goalkeeper Jesus Owono does not deserve the 12-match ban he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

Owono collided with De Miguel in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier match on 2 November, with De Miguel subsequently rushed to intensive care before passing away the morning after in hospital.

Owono, who was sent off for the foul before the match was abandoned, said he was going through “the most difficult days of my life” in the aftermath of De Miguel’s death.

He has since been hit with a lengthy suspension for violent conduct by the Spanish football federation (Rfef), with its disciplinary committee saying he used “excessive force” in the collision.

This has drawn the ire of former Barcelona defender Pique, the majority shareholder of Owono’s club Andorra, who feels the Equatorial Guinea stopper is being punished for the consequences rather than his action.

"Players, ​former ⁠players, coaches, goalkeepers, everyone has called it an accident," Pique remarked in a video posted on social media ⁠late on Monday.

“I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened.”.

Pique notes there is inconsistency in the punishment, citing Albacete winger Jose Corpas’ three-match ban after his high challenge on Sabadell midfielder Quadri Liameed left him hospitalised.

“Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,” he added.

“With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?”.

Andorra general manager Jaume Nogues told Andorra Radio and Television on Tuesday that they would not be appealing the disciplinary committee's decision, but that their resolution on the case was "not done well".

Nogues mentioned an appeal would be "frowned upon socially", adding that Owono was also not in favour of launching an appeal.

Meanwhile, Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera ‌did not agree with Pique's evaluation.

"He has to defend his players and his club, and he clearly believes thats what hes doing," Cervera told a press conference on Tuesday.

In a recent development, "I do think the action [Owono's ⁠challenge] could have been avoided. I don’t believe this is the kind of action ⁠we see every day, despite what he seems to be suggesting.".

Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter.

Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have mentioned that criminal proceedings are unlikely.

Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again, with Pique stating that Owono will live with the repercussions of the incident for much longer than the duration of his 12-game suspension.

Sources indicate that “Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to compete,” he remarked. “No sanction is going to bring [De Miguel] back to us.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics.
  • Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead.
  • Recent findings suggest that the head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics.

Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2. The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before.

Recent findings suggest that the head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he remarked, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards.

Sources indicate that against Mexico, the defender was sent off for a late tackle in the 54th minute with England 2-1 up. Against Spain, he contributed to Elliot Anderson being sent off in the 63rd minute with England 3-0 up. Quansah had his pocket picked by Lamine Yamal and Anderson’s attempt to chase back and rectify the situation ended with him fouling the winger.

According to recent reports, it was not only a red card but a penalty; the prompt for Spain to launch a furious and hitherto unadvertised fightback. It had the stand that housed the press box shaking. Structural integrity was very much a theme.

Sources indicate that as in Mexico, Tuchel made defensive changes. This time, it was Myles Lewis-Skelly for Harry Kane; Djed Spence for Anthony Gordon. Tuchel also withdrew Jude Bellingham, who went off shaking his head. It was easy to understand his frustration. He was excellent. Tuchel had removed his two prime attackers. He also put Dan Burn on towards the end, albeit this time not as part of a back five. England stayed in a 4-4-1 formation, with Quansah moving from central defence to right-back. As in Mexico, the 10-man low block resisted.

According to recent reports, as much as Tuchel disagreed, this felt like Argentina reloaded as well. “No, not at all,” he mentioned, when the World Cup semi-final defeat was raised. “Because of one man down. We would not have been in this situation if it was 11 against 11.”.

It has been revealed that the parallels, nevertheless, were there. Tuchel made defensive substitutions at 1-0 up against Argentina; it was a back five on that occasion. As against Spain, his team could not get out and they faced a flurry of chances. There were other factors in play at the World Cup, chief among them the high levels of fatigue within the squad. England could not hold out, conceding two late goals to exit and bring down a wave of criticism on Tuchel.

It has been revealed that the score is the ultimate takeaway. It can skew analysis. Had Trafford not got back up after parrying a shot from the Spain substitute Fermín López to brilliantly repel Aymeric Laporte’s follow‑up, England would have gone from enjoying a fabulous result to stewing over an opportunity missed. The stakes were nowhere near as high as at the World Cup, but they would have gone from finishing top of their Nations League group to advancing into the quarter-finals as an unseeded second-place team.

In terms of Tuchel’s approach to the closing stages of a big game, what changed?

The truth for England lay in the opening 63 minutes. This was where the evidence of a decisive shift could be found, the reasons for the swell of optimism. England have never played better under Tuchel – and this was against the team to beat; the world and European champions. On their turf.

Recent findings suggest that spain were without the injured Rodri and Dani Olmo, and Luis de la Fuente strangely decided to use Pedri only as a substitute, but their lineup still shimmered with menace; Lamine Yamal was frightening. Yet before their penalty, converted by Mikel Oyarzabal, they did not have a shot on target. Or a real chance.

What stood out from the first whistle was England’s front‑foot intent; the bravery on the ball. They believed they would win and there was a fearlessness about them. They made forward moves on the half turn. There was a slickness about their combinations.

Spain have never suffered like this under De la Fuente and it was everything Tuchel had dreamed of when he started to plot a newly introduced version of his team after the World Cup; a more fluid game model, a response to the Argentina defeat.

Sources indicate that tuchel loved England’s buildup play, which included some of Trafford’s passing. He loved the high press; the aggression in the duels; the threat on set pieces. He stated he loved the low-block defending too. Ben White was excellent at right-back and there was a coming-of-age performance from Lewis Hall at left-back, but it felt wrong to single out individuals.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t stop and I think we are ready to go [like this] for 90 minutes,” Tuchel mentioned. “It was a complete performance and we will not look back now. Go forward and stay hungry. We will not go back on this way of playing that we find ourselves since the World Cup.”.

Ezri Konsa, who headed in the second goal from a Declan Rice corner, remarked England “would have scored two more” if they had kept 11 men on the pitch. “You saw until the red card how much quality we had,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that “We dominated the game. The instruction was to keep going at them. Don’t stop. To keep our foot on the pedal. Argentina was different; different circumstances.”.

Tuchel was asked about the journey from the heartbreak of Argentina to this point; the end of a stirring Nations League group campaign, including the 7-0 win against Croatia in Rijeka. It has not all been super exciting; the 2-1 Wembley win against Croatia last Thursday, for example, was a grind. Was he always confident of a successful reboot?

“It took me a while to digest [the World Cup] and see the way forward,” he stated. “How we can help and adjust and improve? We had reviews and so on but the clarity came in the first Nations League camp [in September and October] with the players.

According to recent reports, “The first week was not so easy. Some players were still upset from the World Cup. Some were upcoming in the team. Some had digested it, some had not. But it was vital to have this process together and everyone committed to wanting to improve in certain aspects of the game.

“We had the energy right to take the next steps and from there we went. Full credit to the players, how they buy in. It’s amazing that it came together like this now.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Angry captain Andy Robertson says Scotland do not have time to turn things around after a brutal 4-0 defeat by Switzerland consigned them to a third-place finish in their Nations League group.

Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli - appointed as Steve Clarke's successor in August - has consistently stressed the need for patience as he tries to implement a more attack-minded style.

However, the Belgian has won just two of his first six matches in charge, both against North Macedonia, and conceded 10 goals in that time.

They collapsed worryingly easily in St Gallen against a much-changed Swiss outfit on Monday after a promising start, Bologna midfielder Lewis Ferguson putting through his own goal and early intensity gave way to indecision.

The Swiss struck twice in the early minutes of the second half to make it 3-0 and Zeki Amdouni made it four late on.

'You do not have time in international football'.

"First half, I thought we were in the game, we lost a stupid goal, but I thought we had chances and could have been 2-1 at half time," a frustrated Robertson said, on the night he surpassed Kenny Dalglish as his country's most capped men's player.

"By the time you get to 50 minutes and you're 3-0 down, that can't happen in international football.

"It is a really tough night for us. I don't think you've got time in international football, you have to do it.

"These supporters who travel everywhere, are they going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden who are going to be critical and rightly so? No.

"We don't have time, the players do not have time, we have got to step up.

"We have a long break now to March, which is not a good thing, and it is going to be a tough one to swallow.".

What's the story with Pocognoli, is it now time to go?

Pocognoli's abject Scotland beaten 4-0 in Switzerland.

Robertson eclipses Dalglish to become Scotland's most capped man.

This was meant to be a special occasion for Robertson, but it was usurped by the debate over Pocognoli's future.

Just six games into his tenure, there are serious questions being asked over whether the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco coach is capable of delivering on his promise of making Scotland easier on the eye, while delivering positive results.

Tottenham Hotspur left-back Robertson was not the only player to deliver a scathing assessment.

When asked if Scotland were on the right path, John McGinn replied: "Well, obviously the trajectory of the results means it's impossible for me to say yes.".

Fellow midfielder Billy Gilmour added: "As a team we know we need to show passion and fight. We've not quite done that tonight.".

Supporters are already frustrated at Pocognoli's 3-5-2 formation as they see wingers sidelined or - in the case of Ben Gannon-Doak - shoehorned into an unfamiliar wing-back role.

One man familiar with the difficulties of being the Scotland manager is former boss Craig Levein, who believes the Belgian needs to take a leaf out of his predecessor's book.

According to recent reports, "Pocognoli is picking up where Clarke left off," Levein said on BBC Scotland. "In that situation, you need to get off to a good start. That's what the players are looking for - that you're going to make them better.

"I'd be thinking 'we need to stop losing goals'. We haven't got a potent threat, so how do we get results? As Steve recognised, you need to be hard to beat.".

In contrast to his deflated players, Pocognoli put on a brave face post-match and insists he sees positive signs after his first two camps.

"The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game," he said.

"We played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments, and we faced Switzerland with different shapes and adapted well from the first minute. We conceded from maybe one of the first chances they had.

"At the end, it's a bad feeling, the score, but I think that the players try to do their best and create moments that we want to see.".

Again Pocognoli called for patience and the time which Robertson notes Scotland do not have.

In a recent development, "The more we have games together, the more we will try to fix these things," the head coach noted. "We have a lot of good response from this camp and it's good for the future as well.".

But whatever Pocognoli's selling, former Scotland winger Pat Nevin isn't buying.

"If I'm ever in trouble and I need a PR man, I'm getting him because he's absolutely good at it," he said on Sportsound.

Sources indicate that "He's certainly a glass-half-full person. You can talk away any moment and say it's just a moment, but it's four moments, five moments, six moments.

It has been revealed that "A really horrible thing in that situation is that if I am running the SFA, I'd be asking the players what they think and just saying 'tell us the truth... are you backing us?'.

"If a couple of the main ones say 'we're not sure of the decision-making' then I think it's got to that stage.".

'Scotland have not played well in any game this campaign'.

In a recent development, fraser: Utter shambles. Embarassing. How can players who play for so called "big" clubs look like they've never seen a football before when they put on a Scotland shirt?

It has been revealed that matt: Six games. Six poor results. Our ranking will tank. And all Clarke's good work will be undone. It's time to admit Mulholland got it wrong. Sometimes you don't need data and metrics to see the simple solution. Poco no more.

Shirleyanne: All these comments about how rubbish we are I would like to know if they are the same people who when we play well are getting in touch praising the team?? The manager needs time, the players need time too.. Yes it's not been great but come on give them a chance and get behind them instead of moaning..

Grant: Pocognoli is the new Russell Martin, talks a good game but is actually clueless and too stubborn to admit his tactics are dire. I did say be careful what you wish for when the gaffer quit in June and this will only end one way so might as well get it done well before March. Someone should call Steve Clarke.

Brett: When you have limited resources like Scotland, you have to utilise them to good effect - take a look at what Michael O'Neil is doing with Northern Ireland, he is getting results. And you can say that Scotland has a better pool of players to choose from than Northern Ireland does, so...

#13155. Tech Report: SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky?

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (904 w)

Tech Report: SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX's Starship megarocket is slated to launch on its ambitious 15th flight test as soon as this Friday (Nov.
  • Flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m.
  • "As it launches towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX's Starship megarocket is slated to launch on its ambitious 15th flight test as soon as this Friday (Nov. 13). Will you be able to spot its leviathan upper stage, known as Ship, or its Starlink satellite passengers as they circle Earth during the historic orbital jaunt?

Flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT) on Nov. 13. Starship will fly from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, where it will be 4:45 p.m. at the opening of the window — about an hour before sunset. The launch could therefore be especially dramatic for folks in the area.

"As it launches towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S. are going to be in Texas and the states along the Gulf of Mexico," Robert Massey, deputy executive director at the Royal Astronomical Society, told Space.com. "They could see the exhaust plume (the 'jellyfish') with the sky darker for observers further east.".

Recent findings suggest that if all goes to plan, Starship's Super Heavy booster will propel the Ship upper stage through the densest part of Earth's atmosphere before returning to Starbase for a powered landing and capture via the "chopstick" arms of the "Mechazilla" tower system. Ship, meanwhile, will go on to orbit Earth approximately 14 times over the following 22 hours, during which time it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before returning to Starbase for its own ambitious catch attempt.

Satellite visibility in the night sky depends on a cocktail of factors, from the size of the spacecraft to its reflectivity, orbital inclination and position relative to the Earth and sun.

Ship is big — about 171 feet (52 meters) tall — so it will be a viable target for skywatchers, experts say.

"It certainly will be visible in twilight hours. It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size," professor James Osborn of Durham University told Space.com. "Where and when is a bit more tricky.".

In a recent development, ship and its Starlink satellites may be seen in the 90 minutes directly after sunset on Nov. 13 and before sunrise on Nov. 14, as the probes catch the sunlight on either side of Earth's colossal shadow as they drift through the twilight sky.

Industry observers note that the spacecraft will initially appear as a string of bright, evenly spaced lights, with Ship most likely appearing significantly brighter than the Starlink satellites. However, Osborn noted that the lack of publicly available data makes it challenging to forecast exactly when the spacecraft will appear.

"During its 14 orbits over 22 hours, the spacecraft is between inclinations of 30.5 [degrees] N and S of the equator," explained Massey. "So it will be best viewed between those latitudes, and then lower in the sky up to latitudes of 40 N and 40 S. That's pretty much the whole of the contiguous U.S.".

Space.com skywatching columnist and veteran meteorologist Joe Rao shared further details on what stargazers may see with the naked eye as Ship drifts silently through the autumn sky.

Industry observers note that "When it passes overhead, it will look like a bright, fast-moving star crossing the sky — similar to the International Space Station, but potentially even brighter depending on its orientation," explained Rao. "The Starlink V3 satellites are much smaller, so not as bright, perhaps ranging anywhere from 2nd to 4th magnitude, depending on the angle of illumination with reflected light from the sun.".

According to recent reports, magnitude is the scale used by astronomers to measure the brightness of objects in the night sky. The lower the magnitude, the brighter the object! The unaided eye can make out objects with a magnitude of around +6.5 under ideal dark sky conditions, while the planet Venus right now shines at magnitude -4.41.

Industry observers note that the Starlink train will likely fall further behind Starship as the 22-hour mission progresses, while the train itself will become more elongated, according to Rao. "For locations where it will make a high arc across the sky, the Starship should be visible for at least a few minutes, although because it is orbiting at a lower altitude (170 miles/275 km) compared to the ISS, it probably will appear to move somewhat faster. ".

There are multiple handy resources that should allow you to track Ship and the newly deployed batch of V3 Starlink satellites following their scheduled launch on Nov. 13, including the websites Heavens-Above, Star Dash, Orbital Radar and Find Starlink.

Be sure to keep an eye on our Starship Flight 15 live blog for all the latest news along with our launch timings article containing details on how to watch SpaceX's potentially historic orbital launch attempt.

Editor's Note: If you capture a photo of Starship and want to share it with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

He has a passion for the night sky, science, Hideo Kojima, and human space exploration, and can’t wait for the day when astronauts once again set foot on the moon.

Manchester United have hired Mauricio Pochettino – and his first transfer demand may break Arsenal hearts.

With the Red Devils languishing in the relegation zone after just three wins in all competitions this season, the Argentine knows that he needs to turn things around swiftly, with January eyed as an opportunity to do business.

And Pochettino could well annoy former team-mate Mikel Arteta with a move he's requested from his bosses at Manchester United.

Pochettino and Arteta know each other well from playing together at Paris Saint-Germain, while the Basque was invited to become a member of Pochettino's staff during his time on the other side of North London, at Tottenham Hotspur.

It's perhaps no surprise then, given their similar outlook on the game, that the fresh United boss has earmarked a long-time Arsenal target as his first signing in the Old Trafford dugout.

Fichajes in Spain have reported that Pochettino has requested the signing of Julian Alvarez after walking through the door at Carrington, with the Gunners well-known admirers.

Arteta spent much of the summer looking to convince the Atletico Madrid man to return to English football and sign for the Premier League champions – with Alvarez himself waiting up until deadline day for a move to Barcelona that never materialised.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The relationship between the Atleti man and their idol hasn't been the same since, and with Barça having moved on from the player and Raphinha thriving in the No.9 role, it appears the pathway to a Camp Nou move is closed.

If Alvarez still wants to leave the Metropolitano, Arsenal would be the sensible destination given their interest and the fact they didn't upgrade either on the left wing or up front over the summer – but interest from United would complicate matters, with Pochettino perhaps able to convince his compatriot he could build around him.

Alvarez was a huge hit during his time in the Premier League, though adored on the blue side of Manchester, where he won a Treble and a World Cup in his first full season as a Manchester City player.

The 26-year-old has continued to flourish under Diego Simeone, scoring 29 goals in all competitions in his first season and 20 the following campaign.

FourFourTwo understands that the finances may not be there for a January move, though with United, nothing should be ruled out.

Alvarez is worth €110 million, according to Transfermarkt. Manchester United face Liverpool when Premier League action resumes this weekend.

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however a win or draw for Northern Ireland against Hungary would see them top Group B2 and be promoted to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.
