📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Thomas Frank decided the Crystal Palace job was “too good to turn down” after talks with chairman Steve Parish.

The 53-year-old Dane, out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February, has spent the last nine months travelling, spending time with family, and reflecting on his career.

He takes charge of what he believes is an “iconic” English club, but one with plenty of work to do if they want to escape the Premier League relegation battle.

Industry observers note that “You know, honestly speaking, I was a little bit, ‘When do I want to go back in? Is it now?’ Then this opportunity came up,” Frank told PalaceTV.

“I was thinking, this is probably too good to turn down for various reasons.”.

Frank’s strong admiration for Eagles supporters – he was at Wembley when Palace lifted the FA Cup – was a contributing factor.

He added: “The second part of it was the very good conversation with Steve Parish. He’s been around, he knows what’s happening, he knows how to run a football club.

“You always say you need to do your due diligence about the one who takes the decisions, and everything I’ve heard about Steve, everything I knew, it was positive, and then on top of that the conversation with Matt Hobbs, Iain Moody, was substantial.

In a recent development, “So all that adding up, looking into the team that I see is extremely exciting, good potential, or just thinking, ‘Hmm, this is interesting’. And when I’m sitting here, walking around the training ground, it was just, ‘Ok, you’re back’, which scared me a little bit, but it’s good.”.

That Hobbs and Moody helped convince Frank to sign a two-and-a-half year deal will, for Palace fans, carry hope that the new boss will be backed in the January transfer window.

The Eagles lost a number of key personnel in the summer from their Conference League-winning squad, including Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea.

Their absence has been felt on a side that has conceded the most goals, 24, in the Premier League.

“To state the obvious, we need to stabilise things,” said Frank, who pointed to defending, set pieces in both boxes, and defensive transitions as priorities to address, beginning with Saturday’s trip to Coventry.

“We need to bring energy, we need to bring belief, we need to bring confidence, because this is a very, very good team with very good players, but they need to believe in themselves.

“We need to balance a lot of things with aiming high in Europe, two fantastic cup tournaments, but of course the Premier League is the most notable if we need to prioritise, but we would like to compete in all things.”.

Frank, who was sacked by Tottenham after a run of only two wins in 17 matches, stated he needed to “re-energise” after that disappointment.

Sources indicate that he travelled to Japan and Australia with his family, spent a rare summer in Denmark, reflected on a relentless decade of work, and started speaking to people to get inspiration. Then, Palace called.

“Timing is everything in football,” he added. “Coming back to the convincing conversation with Steve, Matt and Iain convinced me that this was the right time to come back.”.

#13147. On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (637 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P.
  • Industry observers note that the European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014.
  • When it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P. To say it was a bumpy landing would be an understatement.

Industry observers note that the European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014. It was supposed to use harpoons to secure itself on to the surface of Comet 67P, but the harpoons never fired.

When it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space. The first bounce brought Philae half a mile above the comet's surface before gravity brought it back down.

According to recent reports, philae was missing for almost two years before scientists found it. Images from Rosetta indicated Philae stuck in a dark crevice on top of the rubber duck-shaped comet.

The European Space Agency's Rosetta and Philae expedition was a first-of-its-kind mission, an endeavour to not just rendezvous with a comet and watch it change over time as it approached the sun (that was Rosetta's job), but also to soft-land a probe on its icy and rocky surface to see what a comet is truly made of.

The Rosetta and Philae mission succeeded on both counts, but Philae's historic landing was marred by its turbulent touchdown. Philae actually landed three different times on Comet 67/P, all because the harpoons designed to secure it in place didn't fire as planned.

After the first landing, Philae bounced up and drifted around the comet for two hours, making another bounce before Rosetta's cameras lost track of it. Scientists figured it was stuck in a shady spot where sunlight couldn't reach its solar panels. Because it was solar-powered, Philae needed to be facing the sun properly to generate enough power for sustained operation on the comet's surface.

In a recent development, still, Philae did have some power stored in batteries, which lasted for more than two days on the surface. That allowed Philae to perform some science with its 10 instruments in the time it had on Comet 67/P. Most notably, Philae found organic molecules that had never been detected on a comet before.

Sources indicate that the Rosetta orbiter continued to orbit Comet 67P until September 2016, and it was in that month -- just weeks before Rosetta itself landed on the comet on Sept. 30, 2016 -- that the spacecraft rediscovered the Philae lander lying on its side in a rocky crevice.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

Industry observers note that on this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA releases Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard.

Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from Fresh York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She right now lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jurgen Klopp took over as Germany head coach in July.
  • Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp claims he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.
  • Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jurgen Klopp took over as Germany head coach in July.

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp claims he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.

Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.

Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.

Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the plan but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.

"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," stated former Liverpool boss Klopp.

"I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.".

Klopp added: "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.".

French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo has been named as Uefa's candidate to challenge Infantino.

Diallo received the unanimous support of Uefa's executive committee and formal ratification from the FFF is expected on Tuesday.

Uefa, which is European football's governing body, stated it has "full confidence" Diallo would "uphold the highest standards of governance" amid its calls for "renewed unity and trust within the global football community".

Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino.

Infantino apologises to Fifa Council - but told he is still not fit to lead.

Uefa has been one of Infantino's fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down.

It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts for all documents related to FFE to be released.

The deadline for candidates to officially confirm they are standing against Infantino in Fifa's presidential election is Wednesday.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who is Fifa's head of global development, had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport he has ruled himself out.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also unveiled his intention to stand.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football - people who aren't driven by financial interests," noted Klopp.

"If someone like that were to step up - if someone like that were to become president - I think that would be a significant improvement.

"There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.".

Strasbourg, acquired by Chelsea’s parent company BlueCo in 2023, have identified Matos as a replacement for Oliveira, who has won three of 10 league matches since succeeding Gary O’Neil in July. The French club are hovering two points above the relegation zone.

Matos is under contract until 2030 and Swansea would be due significant compensation for the 38-year-old, a former Liverpool academy and development team coach.

Matos has won admirers since taking charge of Swansea last November and, despite one win in their past five games, has the south Wales club in the Championship playoff spots. Swansea finished last season in 11th and backed Matos in the transfer market this summer in the hope of pushing on.

Swansea’s next match is at home to West Brom on Saturday, before a trip to Middlesbrough and a south Wales derby against Cardiff in the Welsh capital.

In a recent development, matos, who is due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea this month, joined the club from Marítimo, a Portuguese second-division club. His 12-game spell in charge of Maritimo represented his first senior management job.

Strasbourg and Chelsea share a close relationship and have traded players, with Emmanuel Emegha and Valentín Barco joining the English club in recent months.

In the most notable move between the clubs, however, Liam Rosenior left his role as Strasbourg head coach to take charge of Chelsea in January, but the former Hull manager was sacked in April. O’Neil succeeded Rosenior but joined Ipswich in June.

Raya moved to Blackburn Rovers as a teenager and spent a year on loan in the English non-league – so has never experienced his native league, telling the publication, “Perhaps, in the future, I could play for a Spanish club: I’m Spanish, and naturally, I’d love to play there.”.

Despite the interest, and Raya recently turning 31 – making him the second-oldest player in Arteta's squad behind fellow custodian, Kepa Arrizabalaga – Sport Witness have now relayed a report from ESPN regarding the contract situation of four players at London Colney.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026.

It was some night for James Trafford.

As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured a memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.

The Leeds keeper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.

On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches.

Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range.

Last week Tuchel had made it clear that Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford was his number one.

But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match".

So, following his performance on Sunday night, is Trafford now likely to oust Pickford as England's go-to goalkeeper?

Is Trafford 'closing the gap' on Pickford?

In a recent development, despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.

Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a Â£31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for Â£45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.

Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.

At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's big five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).

He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.

Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.

After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice.

Recent findings suggest that "Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him.".

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes.".

After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.

And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management.

"This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing.".

Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard.

According to recent reports, could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.

Pickford - "You've got to respect it".

Industry observers note that what about Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.

The 32-year-old has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.

According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.

And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.

In a recent development, "We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," mentioned former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain,.

In a recent development, "It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.

"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much.

"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection.".

In a recent development, this isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.

60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages.

Sarina Wiegman has recalled Chelsea forward Aggie Beever-Jones and handed two players their first England call-ups ahead of the Lionesses’ World Cup play-off matches against Ukraine.

Beever-Jones, 23, was left out of England’s previous camp in October, when the Lionesses overcame Greece, but she has earned her place back in a 25-player squad named on Tuesday morning.

Injuries to regulars Alex Greenwood and Lauren James have forced them out of the team while forward Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox have both been handed maiden senior call-ups.

It has been revealed that on London City Lionesses star Goodwin, Wiegman noted: “I think she has done well. We always know she’s a huge talent, high potential. She demonstrated that over a couple of games. So we want to see her in our environment.

“She has some different qualities. She’s really fast too. She has length, she can head and she can score goals.”.

Grace Fisk, Freya Godfrey, Erica Meg Parkinson and Lexi Potter all made their debuts in October’s 8-1 two-legged round one rout over Greece and have kept their places in the squad this time.

London City Lionesses left-back Poppy Pattinson, who made her debut against Ukraine in March, has been recalled.

Arsenal forward Chloe Kelly continues to miss out and there is no place for Lucia Kendall while Manchester United’s Ella Toone keeps her place in the squad after she originally missed out on being named in October’s internationals.

Speaking on Toone, Wiegman stated: “She responded really well, working really hard.

“She came in our camp and was ready also straight away. Going back to her club, she’s done well too and that’s what has been fed back to me.”.

Wiegman’s side are just one step away from securing their place at next summer’s World Cup in Brazil, needing to beat Ukraine in round two of the play-offs.

England will travel to Murcia on Tuesday 1 December for the away fixture before they host the second leg at Wembley Stadium four days later.

The upcoming fixtures will be England’s first since head coach Wiegman signed a contract extension until the conclusion of Euro 2029.

  • Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.

A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered.

When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices.

Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.

"For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis," Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville remarked in a statement.

Several other supernova imposters have been observed over the past decade or two. Until now, no one knew what causes these stars to repeatedly cry wolf. Thanks to Chandra’s X-ray vision, Aghakhanloo has led a team of astronomers who think they have now uncovered an explanation.

The supernova imposter is named AT 2016blu, and is a type of star that we call a 'luminous blue variable,' or LBV. These are the most massive and luminous stars in the universe and their extreme characteristics result in them being highly unstable, undergoing intermittent bouts of mass loss as they eject material from their outer layers into the surrounding space.

However, faking a supernova is not part of their typical behavior, so a newly introduced way of looking at AT 2016blu was needed.

"To understand the cause of these eruptions, we realized that we needed X-ray data that was timed so that we’d observe the star when it was in an outburst," team member Núria Torres-Albà, also from the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, noted.

Industry observers note that aghakhanloo’s team were granted the opportunity to commandeer Chandra to target an outburst of AT 2016blu at the earliest opportunity. That opportunity arose in March 2026.

Industry observers note that chandra had previously and coincidentally looked in the direction of NGC 4559 back in 2001 and 2002 and did not notice anything unusual back then. This time around, however, it captured a powerful blast of X-rays coinciding with yet another false supernova outburst.

Recent findings suggest that the X-ray detection allowed Aghakhanloo’s team to assemble a picture of what is happening. "Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen," he mentioned.

Chandra’s X-ray observations indicate that AT 2016blu has an unseen companion, a compact, high-gravity object that is either a neutron star or a stellar-mass black hole on an elliptical 113-day orbit around the luminous blue variable.

Neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes are the core remnants of massive stars that have gone supernova for real, meaning that at one time AT 2016blu was a binary star system.

Each time the compact object reaches the point in its orbit that is closest to the luminous blue variable, its powerful gravity is able to pull material from the unstable star. This sets in motion a chain of events that results in the brilliant outbursts.

As the stolen starstuff is dragged away from the wounded star and towards the compact object, it forms an accretion disk swirling around the neutron star or black hole so fast and growing so hot that it emits X-rays. These are the X-rays that Chandra saw.

Sources indicate that the X-rays are immense, energizing the surrounding cloud of material that had been ejected by the luminous blue variable years before. The cloud is heated and glows extremely brightly in visible light, creating the impression of a supernova.

Recent findings suggest that "We suspected that the bright repeating flashes at optical wavelengths might actually be powered by periodic blasts of high-energy X-rays," said team member Nathan Smith of the University of Arizona in Tucson. "The dense gas surrounding the system is heated by the X-rays and then glows in the optical.".

It has been revealed that calculations suggest that each year a 440 billion trillion pounds of material at minimum is stolen by the compact object, and possibly two orders of magnitude more than that. This is a huge amount, yet it is only 800 millionths of the mass of the sun, and AT 2016blu’s luminous blue variable is at least 33 times the mass of the sun.

Nevertheless, it is far greater than the maximum rate of material that a neutron star can safely accrete, referred to as the Eddington limit. It’s little wonder that the accretion onto the compact object unleashes such extreme energies.

In a recent development, AT 2016blu is also connected with another mysterious and rare astrophysical phenomenon, that of ultra-luminous X-ray (ULX) sources. The identity of whatever it is that is powering ULXs remains unclear, but the involvement of compact objects such as black holes and neutron stars is high on the list.

Industry observers note that AT 2016blu is bright enough to be considered a ULX, so could it act as a Rosetta stone connecting supernova imposters with ULXs? It’s too early to say that; only one other supernova impostor has so far been found to have X-ray emission typical of material being stolen from one star and accreting onto a compact body, and that is SN 2010da, but in that case it is known that the companion is another massive star, a red supergiant, rather than a compact object.

According to recent reports, the X-ray detection of AT 2016blu is described in a paper published on Monday (Nov. 9) in The Astrophysical Journal.

Keith Cooper is a freelance science journalist and editor in the United Kingdom, and has a degree in physics and astrophysics from the University of Manchester. He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.

“At a meeting held today and chaired by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the Uefa executive committee and the Fifa council invited Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support,” a statement stated.

Recent findings suggest that diallo emerged as the favourite after plans to enlist a decorated former player or manager did not reach fruition. Uefa stated the 63‑year‑old had accepted the invitation and that his candidacy was due to be ratified on Tuesday by the FFF.

Diallo strongly criticised Infantino in September, saying: “His initiatives during and after the World Cup have seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”.

Sources indicate that it is unclear whether the move to back Diallo will spell the end of the campaign begun by Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, to challenge Infantino. Tashima, a Fifa council member, has influential backers within Uefa but its hierarchy appears to feel Diallo has a greater chance of wooing voters in other areas of the world.

There are concerns that having multiple challengers to Infantino will strengthen his position and play into the hands of a campaign that will present the incumbent as the unity candidate after months of infighting.

Northern Ireland play Hungary in Budapest needing a point for Nations League promotion.

With six of his starting outfield players against Ukraine on Saturday night having gone into the game a yellow card away from suspension, it was always likely that Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill would need to reshuffle his team for the Nations League Group B2 finale in Hungary.

That the player who picked up the booking ended up being Jamie Donley, however, has presented the boss with something of a selection conundrum.

The Tottenham Hotspur forward, presently on loan at Luton Town, has started the side's past 10 games at centre-forward, a different role to the deeper position he has more usually occupied in his club career.

With O'Neill having circled through traditional number nine options such as Dion Charles, Jamie Reid and Lee Bonis since returning to the job four years ago, it feels as if Donley has made the shirt his own since being handed the start against Luxembourg 12 months ago.

While the manager has pushed back on the idea that Donley is playing out of position at international level, the one-game ban is certainly an untimely one with the former Leyton Orient and Oxford United loanee's hold-up play in particular against Ukraine showing how much he has grown into the role.

After the 21-year-old had a goal chalked off by the video assistant referee (VAR) on Saturday, he has still scored just once from open play for his country, but there is a growing appreciation that he is asked to bring much more than just goals to the team.

"He's been such a good player for us. Even without the goals, the way he holds the ball up and spreads the play, his movement is just so good. Playing balls in the air, he pins the defender so well," mentioned Fulham midfielder Shea Charles.

"He's got better every game and he's like the perfect player for us.".

Tuesday, 17 November at 19:45 GMT.

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC One NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website.

There is no obvious like-for-like replacement in O'Neill's squad for a game in which they need a draw to secure promotion to Nations League A for the first time.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill pulled out of the double-header through injury last week, with Josh Magennis, Callum Marshall and the uncapped pair of Eoin Kenny and Braiden Graham the other strikers in the travelling party.

Similar to the original ask of Donley, there is also an option to move a wide or deeper player such as Isaac Price or Paddy Kelly into a central striking role.

With only three days between games, however, there has been little time to work on such a plan to replace a player whose four Spurs appearances all came under Ange Postecoglou in the 2023-24 season.

"There are other things we can do. We can change the shape a little bit, play with two front players," noted O'Neill, who himself is suspended for the game after two bookings and will watch from the stands.

Recent findings suggest that "There's a number of things that we will look at. Obviously the time between the games makes that somewhat more difficult in terms of preparation.

"We'll find hopefully the right player that can first of all fit into what we want to do, but obviously secondly give the opposition some problems as well.".

Nobody in O'Neill's squad has more international caps or goals than Stevenage striker Magennis.

But while the 36-year-old has started 11 games in League One this season, it has been more than three years since he last did so at international level.

"My role has obviously changed since I've come into the squad," remarked the player with 94 international appearances and 12 goals to his name.

"If Michael wants to play with the target man and with experience, obviously, he's going to go for me. If he wants a like-for-like, he's probably going to go with Marshy [Callum Marshall]. So, me and Marshy will probably play rock, paper, scissors.

According to recent reports, "Jamie brings so much to the team, but I don't think there's going to be a drastic downfall if one of us has to step in for us. I think the competition for places in the squad for us is absolutely brilliant and if you get that opportunity, you've just got to take it.".

It has been revealed that that means that Man of Tomorrow, which arrives next summer, will be the final entry in Gunn's ambitious, and occasionally divisive, DC experiment. The DCU's first chapter — officially titled 'Gods and Monsters' — gave us Supergirl and Clayface (as well as TV shows like Peacemaker S2 and Lanterns) in the run-up to Clark Kent and Lex Luthor's return.

Man of Tomorrow looks to be upping the stakes from Earthly villains to intergalactic baddies with the introduction of Brainiac, and it may well have been the herald of the first Justice League movie in the rebooted DCU.

Industry observers note that gunn has yet to prove audiences actually care about more than Batman and Supes, which might explain why this follow-up is also an ensemble of sorts. As the Marvel Cinematic Universe prepares to unleash Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars, and even a fresh X-Men reboot, their DC counterparts have always struggled to get their dream team off the ground.

We'll never know what might have been, but we can still enjoy Gunn's DC swansong when it lands in 2027. Here's everything we know about James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow.

According to recent reports, man of Tomorrow will be released theatrically in the United States on July 9, 2027. Most international territories are expected to get it around the same time.

Only a few months after Superman's release and successful box office run, DC Studios and Warner Bros. Pictures confirmed the sequel would be coming two years after Clark Kent's return to the major screen.

Man of Tomorrow isn't out yet, but you can watch the rest of the DCU so far (it's pretty good for the most part) in preparation first.

When the movie hits theaters on July 9, 2027, it'll likely remain exclusive to substantial screens for at least two or three months, depending on how successful it is.

According to recent reports, with that said, we know Warner Bros. (now part of Skydance) isn't the most patient when it comes to theatrical runs based on its track record, so the chances are Man of Tomorrow will hit HBO Max sooner rather than later, probably by early autumn 2027.

In typical comic book fashion (and somewhat reminiscent of Thor: The Dark World), the main hook in Man of Tomorrow appears to be a reluctant alliance between the first movie's villain, Lex Luthor, and Kal-El (aka Clark Kent). "Enemies to allies" is always a fun dynamic to have in a sequel, especially when stars David Corenswet (Superman) and Nicholas Hoult (Lex Luthor) delivered strong and memorable performances the first time around.

The actual plot remains under wraps, but we can guess Brainiac — one of DC's biggest and most iconic alien villains — will be a tough nut to crack, thus requiring some sort of unofficial team-up that will include returning heroes like Mister Terrific, Guy Gardner, Hawkgirl, John Stewart, Blue Beetle, and even Kara Zor-El (Supergirl). There are other names circling the project that could lead to even bigger appearances, but don't expect to learn much about them before the movie's marketing kicks off.

In a recent development, why should you care about Brainiac? Well, he's a super-intelligent techno-organic alien from the planet Colu with an obsession with knowledge and self-improvement. A perfect foe for Luthor, Earth's greatest mind, but also a breath of fresh air for Superman, who's been stuck battling either Kryptonian menaces or just Luthor too long on the big screen.

Much of the current Man of Tomorrow speculation centers on Adria Arjona's role in the story. While many have theorized she could be playing Wonder Woman — something that neither Gunn nor Arjona has straight-up denied — the earlier reports and rumors suggested she could be Maxima.

Recent findings suggest that such a role would fit Gunn's penchant for throwing lesser-known comic book heroes and villains into his movies wherever possible. She's also morally ambiguous, at least when she first appeared, so that makes her a particularly interesting character to bring in for a more complex and nuanced sequel.

Yes, James Gunn is the sole writer and director of Man of Tomorrow.

In fact, it seems he had already begun working on his next movie after Man of Tomorrow, though his unceremonious exit will almost certainly mean the end of those aims.

He's also co-producing alongside Peter Safran, who was also ousted in November 2026's DC Studios shakeup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jürgen Klopp’s side make statement with 5-0 triumph.

Dutch advance, Greece miss out despite win over Serbia.

Florian Wirtz scored twice as Germany delivered a 5-0 rout of the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday, reaching the Nations League quarter-finals as group winners.

Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists, with Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also on the scoresheet as the hosts delivered their most impressive display so far under Jürgen Klopp’s leadership.

It was Germany’s biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959, and the Netherlands’ first defeat since Xavi Hernández took over as coach in August. The Dutch have still advanced to the last eight by finishing second, with Germany’s fifth goal taking Klopp’s side into top spot.

Sources indicate that the visitors had the first good chance when Jurriën Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away. Germany then went close as the Berlin native Scherhant hit a post after connecting with a cross from his Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu.

Industry observers note that nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same spot and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the far post. Germany pushed for more goals after the break, and Wirtz delivered with a superb solo effort on the hour, lifting a shot in off the left post from the edge of the penalty area.

Schlotterbeck headed in from Gruda’s free-kick with 65 minutes gone, and the RB Leipzig winger laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered home from close range. Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off a post.

Wirtz remarked: “We don’t mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly … We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we’ve taken some great steps in our development as a team.”.

“Everyone will go home with a smile on their face – and for at least the next three or four months, no-one will be questioning the German national team,” Klopp stated afterwards. “Instead, they’ll be thinking: ‘This could really turn into something.’ We have wonderful footballers, great characters … the lads are even surprising themselves.”.

In a recent development, greece had to settle for third place in Group A2 despite a 1-0 home win over Serbia. Giorgos Masouras scored the second-half winner in Volos, but the hosts missed out on a quarter-final place on head-to-head goal difference, their 7-0 defeat by the Netherlands on Friday proving costly. As group winners, Germany will be seeded in Friday’s draw and will avoid England, France and the winners of Group A4 – probably Portugal – in the last eight.

Sources indicate that switzerland completed a dominant campaign in Group B1 by thrashing Scotland 4-0 in St Gallen. Slovenia finished second in the group, claiming a promotion/relegation playoff place, as Danijel Sturm’s double helped them secure a 3-0 win over North Macedonia.

Max Dowman (pictured) became England Under-21s’ youngest-ever goalscorer by grabbing the late winner in a 3-2 friendly victory over France at Ashton Gate.

Lee Carsley’s side made a lightning start as Tottenham's Mikey Moore gave England an early lead on his first under-21s start. Divin Mubama doubled their lead with a header as Ethan Nwaneri set up both of the hosts' first-half goals.

The Young Lions looked comfortable but Tommy Setford allowed France to pull a goal back after he let Giovani Versini’s cross slip through his fingers. The French winger equalised in style moments later, scoring with a shot from distance.

Industry observers note that carsley had handed a first start to promising Arsenal youngster Dowman and he proved to be the hero, tapping in from Harrison Armstrong's pass to give England the win at only 16 years old. Press Association.

In League C, the Faroe Islands beat Moldova 1-0 to complete an unbeaten campaign and earn a playoff place. Slovakia, already guaranteed Group C3 top spot, earned a 2-2 draw with Kazakhstan thanks to Adrian Kapralik’s last-gasp leveller.

According to recent reports, iceland finished Group C4 unbeaten with a 3-0 home victory against Luxembourg securing first place. Second-placed Estonia beat Bulgaria 2-1 to book a playoff spot.

In League D, Gibraltar earned a 1-1 home draw with Malta thanks to Carlos Richards’s late equaliser, while Lithuania defeated Liechtenstein 2-1 in Kaunas.

#13123. Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (474 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (474 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

According to recent reports, want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Gianni Infantino will face a challenge from French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo in next year's Fifa presidential election.

National association representatives on Uefa's executive committee have invited Diallo to stand and given him their unanimous backing.

Recent findings suggest that uefa said Diallo will stand and this was formally ratified following an executive committee meeting at the French Football Federation’s headquarters in Paris on Tuesday. The move follows Arsene Wenger ruling himself out of a challenge to Infantino over the weekend.

Uefa pledged in August to identify a credible alternative candidate to Infantino. That pledge came after the body mentioned it had lost confidence in the Swiss over his initiative to seek private investment in a tech giant to run the commercial aspects of the World Cup and other Fifa competitions.

A Uefa statement said: "Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of Fifa, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community.

“They also called for a Fifa that places the development of the game in every region of the world at the heart of its mission, upholds the highest standards of governance and works in close partnership with its member associations, confederations and football stakeholders. They expressed their full confidence in Philippe Diallo to provide the leadership needed to achieve this ambition.”.

Diallo, who stated he wasn’t initially intending to enter the presidential race, indicates he wants to restore what is now “broken” trust in football’s governance after Infantino seemed to act alone in his privatisation intends, while the creation of a peace prize for US president Donald Trump and the Folarin Balogun red card debacle also sparked huge concerns.

“It created a situation this summer whereby the trust placed in Fifa and it’s president was broken," Diallo noted. “They have damaged the image of football and have introduced the poison of division.”.

Diallo faces a tough challenge to unseat Infantino, who will be standing for a fourth term as Fifa president.

Infantino appeared to be on the ropes in August when his private investor blueprint was rejected by three continents and a number of key allies expressing their concern at how it had been developed.

He has since rallied support, however, and is expected to receive strong backing in Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America.

Japanese FA honorary president Kozo Tashima had earlier declared his intention to stand, as has former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega.

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has called for a change of leadership in Fifa, claiming Infantino compares unfavourably to his predecessor Sepp Blatter, who resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption.

In quotes reported by the BBC, Klopp said: "I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense.

“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.”.

Klopp added: “Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.”.

Leeds United defender Tarik Muharemovic has emerged as one of the Premier League’s most complete centre-backs this season, ranking alongside Arsenal’s Gabriel and Ezri Konsa, and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.

Data published by football analytics platform Ballity Insight Lab evaluated 54 qualifying Premier League centre-backs across the opening 10 league games of 2026/27, plotting each player’s percentile rank across two criteria: front-foot 'stopper' centre-backs and the more disciplined 'covering' centre-backs.

In the model, a stopper is measured by their ability to step out of the defensive line and win the ball, encompassing tackles, aerial duels, clearances and interceptions. Conversely, a covering centre-back is judged on positional security and composure, factoring in ball retention, recoveries and an avoidance of errors.

Out of the 54 central defenders assessed, only four sit inside the top-right quadrant reserved for players who excel at both covering and stopping. Alongside established title contenders Van Dijk and Gabriel, as well as England international Konsa, sits Elland Road favourite Muharemovic.

The numbers underline just how consistently the Bosnia-Herzegovina international has performed at the heart of Leeds’ backline. Muharemovic sits comfortably around the 77th percentile in both the stopper and cover pools, demonstrating an ability to step aggressively into challenges while also sweeping up danger in transition.

Recent findings suggest that stopper or Cover? Premier League centre-backs 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 🛑 Stopper CB: steps out and wins the ball. Tackles, aerials, clearances, interceptions and duels. 🧠 Cover CB: rarely beaten and keeps the ball. Dribble avoidance, ball retention, recoveries and few errors. Needs a stopper as a partner 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Hill, 🇳🇱 Botman and 🇧🇷 Murillo stop, but don’t cover. Needs a cover as a partner.November 16, 2026.

He keeps elite firm at the top end of the chart with Liverpool skipper Van Dijk still leading the cover metric near the 98th percentile while posting around an 80th-percentile stopper score.

Konsa hovers near the 92nd percentile for covering and 88th for stopping, and Arsenal’s Gabriel posts roughly 83rd-percentile marks across both categories.

It has been revealed that just as striking is the calibre of Premier League defenders who fall outside that dual-threat bracket. Several household names are classified as being better covering central defenders than stoppers, meaning they thrive at reading the game and keeping possession, but rely on a more aggressive partner to engage attackers directly.

Manchester City’s Ruben Dias and Marc Guehi, as well as Tottenham Hotspur’s Micky van de Ven all fall into that zone.

Muharemovic’s capacity to bridge both roles has proven invaluable for Leeds so far this season, and the Whites have established themselves as a tricky team to beat.

Whether it be winning first contacts against physical Premier League strikers or dropping off to snuff out balls over the top, the Bosnian's balanced skillset allows Leeds to pair him flexibly across their central defensive trio.

In a division where most central defenders lean heavily toward one side of the game, rubbing shoulders with Van Dijk and Gabriel is a ringing endorsement of Muharemovic’s rapid acclimatisation at Elland Road.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few short months ago, Craig Mulholland, the Scottish FA's chief football officer, and Ian Maxwell, the association's chief executive, spoke about the worldwide search for a newly introduced Scotland head coach.

The data, the metrics, the cosmic input from the analytics company whose input was received at Hampden as if written on tablets of stone.

Recent findings suggest that the process all pointed to Sebastien Pocognoli being their guy. They paraded him around Hampden, told everybody that loads of clubs were on his tail but that they won the chase.

They may, or may not, have mentioned the word 'coup' but that was certainly what their body language was telling you.

For coup, read boo, the sound surely reverberating around the Tartan Army right now after Monday's 4-0 defeat by Switzerland.

Some nonsense has been written about Pocognoli being on twice the salary that Steve Clarke was on, but whatever they're paying him, there's no value in it so far.

In a recent development, money is a factor here. Clarke's three qualifications brought a rich bounty into the SFA's coffers, many millions even after deductions. That cash gave the association a little more opportunity to do some of the things they want to do in grassroots football.

Industry observers note that A world where Scotland miss out on major championships and the financial windfalls that come with qualification is not a place they want to revisit. The next Euros looks like a gimme - almost harder not to qualify than qualify - but the sense of drift in this team is alarming and can't go on much longer.

Mulholland, Maxwell and let's throw SFA president Mike Mulraney into the mix, should be feeling mightily nervous.

Pocognoli wants patience but Scotland 'don't have time' claims Robertson.

Pocognoli's abject Scotland suffer 4-0 Nations League defeat in Switzerland.

Robertson eclipses Dalglish to become Scotland's most capped man.

Most people understood that Pocognoli needed time, but implicit in that understanding was a need to see something developing under him, a burgeoning style of play, some positives here and there, a few signs that even though things might not be great today or tomorrow, they're inching in the right direction.

There's been none of that. Decent players look lost. Pocognoli's system has made Scotland a disjointed soft touch. Structural discipline collapses too often. Players charge forward and leave space in behind. He wants hard pressing and maximum intensity, but his players don't look capable of providing it.

In six games they have scored five goals - two from the penalty spot. Promises of jam tomorrow are not cutting it. People can see a team on the slide.

In Switzerland, there was a drubbing that piles the heat on the Belgian, on the people who appointed him and on the players, too.

'You do not have time in international football'.

If the chaos on the field wasn't a bad enough look for Pocognoli, then some of the words said in the wake of this objectionable 4-0 pummelling to a Switzerland B side playing in third gear only made things worse.

Andy Robertson, on the night he became Scotland's most capped player in history, delivered a damning riff that sounded strongly like a commentary on this coaching regime and this set of players.

Recent findings suggest that in his stead, John McGinn did much the same thing. "You don't get time" was the gist. Who doesn't get time?

Industry observers note that robertson and McGinn didn't lay it on the line, but their thoughts resembled distress flares. These Scotland players can be overhyped, but they are better than some of the nonsense they dished up in St Gallen.

More than one former Scotland international reckoned they saw players not exactly busting a gut out there. These guys know the tell-tale signs.

Some private conversations between the SFA hierarchy and the senior operators in this team need to take place. What were they suggesting in the post-match? What are they really thinking?

An honesty session behind closed doors needs to take place long before the qualification campaign for the next Euros begins in March.

Pocognoli comes across as a good person: open, communicative, passionate and hard-working.

He also appears stubborn in the way he sets up his team, a system that is so easily exploited by more experienced coaches, people like Switzerland boss Murat Yakin, who was missing a battalion of heavy hitters and yet still won this game at a canter.

Yakin started six players who had six caps or fewer to their name - three of them scored.

McGinn stated later that Scotland were in this movie before in the early days of Clarke's tenure, mentioning the 4-0 loss to Russia in 2019 - four goals conceded in 27 minutes.

In a recent development, the difference between Clarke and Pocognoli is obvious. Clarke had vast experience and the nous to fix the problems. Pocognoli is a young coach with no such back story, no such track record in turning bad situations into good.

Pocognoli mentioned later that people should look beyond the result, to the "attitude of the players" who were at times "brilliant, brave and on the front foot".

In a recent development, he argued that 4-0 wasn't a true reflection of the game, referring to the glaring misses by Lewis Ferguson and Scott McTominay. Scotland were 3-0 down at the time. He didn't think the loss had anything to do with a system or a lack of confidence or a lack of belief.

In a recent development, not many fans were buying what he was selling. Listening to some of his players, you doubted that they were buying it either.

In a recent development, after the home loss to Slovenia, Robertson said his team had been "out-played" and "out-fought." There were some other comments made after the desperately stodgy 2-1 win over North Macedonia on Friday. On Monday, it cranked up another level.

It has been revealed that mcGinn was asked if he felt Scotland were on the right path. "Impossible for me to say yes," he replied. It was hard to listen to what the players were trying to say and conclude that everybody's on the same page in this set-up.

Intransigence is not a good characteristic for any manager. In recent times we've seen a few bosses at significant clubs who were wedded to their principles. Russell Martin and Wilfried Nancy didn't last long at Rangers and Celtic.

To repeat Robertson's line, you don't get time.

According to recent reports, clarke had an instinctive understanding of that and pragmatism was his way of taking his team forward, difficult yard by difficult yard. Rigid idealism is not a sensible way to operate, but Pocognoli has gone down that road in his first six games.

It's a dead-end down there. He needs to turn back and find another way while he still can. If he still can.

'Scotland have not played well in any game this campaign'.

A match that should have been about 103 was instead about four. Andy Robertson is due acclaim for becoming the most capped player in Scotland’s history but how the full-back will wish the moment had arrived in different circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that A second-string Switzerland team pulled Scotland apart, raising further and significant questions about the suitability of Sébastien Pocognoli to carry out the job his paymasters boldly entrusted him with. Scottish FA giddiness about Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke, a hugely successful leader of the national team, is looking increasingly ridiculous. “I don’t think you’ve got time in international football,” stated Robertson as dust settled here. Ouch.

This was a horrible night for Pocognoli, who is under serious pressure just three months into his tenure. Scotland’s players looked a disillusioned and disorganised lot. Pocognoli has never previously managed in international football, which renders it reasonable to ask his qualifications to improve this grim scenario. Scotland have finished a distant third in a favourable Nations League section. Ramifications exist for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in December. Pocognoli is taking a pounding in the court of public opinion.

“The score is painful,” remarked Pocognoli. “I see a lot of good things in the way that we try to play. The result is heavy but the players gave everything. They enjoy playing like this.” An eye test suggests otherwise. Scotland are overly generous in defence, lame in midfield and powder-puff in attack. It is quite the mix.

Industry observers note that pocognoli’s demeanour during pre-match media duties suggested he was irritated by the early questioning of his approach. The Belgian is unwilling to deviate from the deployment of three centre-backs whether Scotland are at home to North Macedonia or away to Switzerland. While the prospect of facing a highly impressive Swiss team would ordinarily make Scots gulp, there was cause for hope in St Gallen. Not only had Switzerland already won Group B1 but they were in makeshift form.

Switzerland’s lack of cohesion was apparent during an opening spell where the visitors looked decent. A flurry of set pieces and a John McGinn half volley that dipped over Yvon Mvogo’s crossbar emphasised Scottish attacking intent. On a difficult pitch, Switzerland’s first 20 minutes lacked purpose. As good as things were to get for Scotland, alas.

It has been revealed that there appeared no real danger as Zachary Athekame fired in a hopeful cross from the Swiss right. Scotland had an abundance of cover inside their own penalty area. The problem was that one of those charged with clearing lines, Lewis Ferguson, instead poked the ball past Angus Gunn. No own goals are pretty; this one was especially ugly. Ferguson had needlessly panicked.

It has been revealed that scotland attempted an immediate response as Aaron Hickey headed wide. The Brentford man had to be withdrawn before the interval, apparently damaging his left hamstring when making a defensive intervention.

According to recent reports, hickey, whose career has been seriously disrupted by injury, was understandably distraught. Although Switzerland were by now in control, McGinn spurned a glorious opportunity five minutes before the interval when heading straight at Mvogo. Adrian Bajrami spared McGinn’s blushes with an even worse miss at the opposite end before the teams headed for their orange wedges. The half had been humdrum in nature.

In a recent development, ferguson shanking the ball out for a Switzerland corner set the tone for a spell where the game was put firmly out of Scotland’s reach. Samuel Ballet burst forward from midfield before playing a one-two with Remo Freuler and slamming towards the Scotland net. The ball was heading in before Winsley Boteli made certain, with the video assistant referee dismissing Scotland’s appeals for offside. The ease with which Ballet evaded those in navy blue was as striking as the space Freuler found himself in. Scotland’s structure, once a staple, was nonexistent. Five defenders and two deep lying midfielders were being gleefully ignored by the rampaging Swiss.

Recent findings suggest that number three was another Scotland horror show. Nathan Patterson was dispossessed by Boteli. The forward found Alvyn Sanches, who angled a shot across Gunn. So, so easy. Gunn’s positioning was questionable.

Recent findings suggest that scott McTominay, again peripheral, slammed over when it looked easier to notch a Scotland consolation. Scottish fans jeered after one sideways pass too many in defence. Many headed for the exit as Zeki Amdouni’s shot deflected off Luke Graham and beyond Gunn.

A year ago, Scotland were celebrating World Cup qualification on the most epic of Hampden Park nights as Denmark were vanquished. It is so difficult to square that occasion with 90 minutes in St Gallen. Scotland look a team in ghastly regression.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that spaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov.
  • Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, update for 6:25 p.m. ET: SpaceX has debuted the Starship Flight 15 mission, but did skip the first stage Super Heavy booster landing. See launch video and our full Starship Flight 15 liftoff wrap.

Recent findings suggest that spaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live.

Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX intends to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before.

Industry observers note that you can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan.

Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight.

The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the manufacturer has remarked.

SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy, pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover.

So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX.

"If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description.

The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit.

The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28.

It has been revealed that ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff.

In a recent development, there's no guarantee things will go according to strategy, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile.

It has been revealed that so it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Gianni Infantino remains in a strong position to secure a further four-year mandate as Fifa president, even after enduring significant pushback over his governance.

Industry observers note that however, a number of challengers have stepped forward ahead of next March’s election. So, who is in the running to potentially oust Infantino, and do they realistically have a chance of beating him?

To be eligible, candidates require backing from at least five member associations and must demonstrate active involvement as a player or official within Fifa, a confederation or a national association for two of the preceding five years.

Recent findings suggest that every one of Fifa's 211 member associations holds a single vote, meaning national size or historical success carries no extra weight. Consequently, world champions Spain possess identical voting power to San Marino, who sit bottom of the world rankings.

When two or fewer contenders stand, victory requires a simple majority - exceeding 50 per cent - of the valid votes submitted.

In races with three or more candidates, a two-thirds majority of present and eligible member associations is needed in the initial round. Should subsequent ballots be required, the candidate receiving the fewest votes is knocked out in each round until two remain.

Formal nominations close on Wednesday, four months prior to the assembly. Voting will subsequently occur during the 77th Fifa Congress in Rabat on 18 March.

The Fifa general secretariat is required to inform member associations of the official candidates for president no later than one month before the Congress convenes.

Discontent mounted following proposals for the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), an initiative designed to introduce private funding into a fresh entity overseeing commercial rights for premier Fifa tournaments, such as the World Cup.

Opponents targeted both the structural details of the initiative and the absence of consultation and openness with which it was introduced to Fifa's membership.

The backlash grew so severe that prominent administrators urged Infantino to step down, while multiple regional confederations formed a united front, prompting the president to eventually scrap the plan.

Having withdrawn the FFE plan following threats from European body Uefa to boycott Fifa fixtures, Infantino offered an apology to the Fifa Council regarding the management of the proposal.

While Uefa - among three confederations that had demanded his resignation - remained unmoved, the apology served to mend bridges with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

AFC head Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who had denounced the project as a "fundamental breach of trust", subsequently changed position to offer his endorsement to the president.

Elsewhere, South American governing body Conmebol declined to demand Infantino's departure, while the Confederation of African Football (CAF) maintained solid backing.

A pledge by Infantino to distribute $25m to every member association also seems to have been instrumental in smoothing over tensions.

Sources indicate that concacaf, representing North America, Central America and the Caribbean, originally aligned with Uefa and the AFC in voicing opposition. However, its delegation has since split, with Mexico alongside various Caribbean nations rallying behind Infantino.

As one of the most seasoned figures in the race, Tashima has outlined ambitions to reform Fifa's governance, rebuild institutional accountability and tackle what he views as an unhealthy centralisation of authority.

Possessing deep internal knowledge of the governing body's inner workings, the Japanese administrator offers a direct proposition: "I'll keep what's good and change what's bad.".

Diallo entered the contest relatively late, gathering support from Uefa member associations sitting on both its executive committee and the Fifa Council.

In a recent development, in charge of the FFF since 2023, the Frenchman has consistently challenged Infantino's leadership. Nonetheless, Uefa has stopped short of confirming unanimous backing from its 55 member nations, leaving his exact level of support uncertain.

Vega grounds his platform in athletic credentials, commercial background and ten years of global campaigning, with the former defender stating he has travelled to over 140 nations to build support.

His bid is far from impulsive given his prior campaigns for office, yet three prior failures create doubts over whether his ambitions can translate into meaningful voting power.

Latest Update: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (786 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov.
  • The manufacturer's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms.
  • Sources indicate that on Thursday (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic.

The manufacturer's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms.

Sources indicate that on Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The manufacturer shared photos of the move on X, and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic.".

The phrase is familiar to fans of Douglas Adams' sci-fi classic "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy": In the novel, the electronic guidebook that helps travelers find their way across the cosmos has "Don't panic!" on its cover.

Industry observers note that and Ship 42 itself is connected to the beloved book, by virtue of its serial number. In "The Hitchhiker's Guide," a supercomputer named Deep Mind is asked to come up with "the answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything." It thinks for 7.5 million years and comes up with "42.".

SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has voiced his affection for "The Hitchhiker's Guide" in the past — and he has already paid tribute to it with a well-placed "Don't panic.".

The debut launch of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket back in February 2018 sent Musk's red Tesla Roadster into orbit around the sun, with a spacesuit-clad mannequin named Starman at the wheel and its entertainment display programmed to read "Don't panic!".

Starship Flight 15 is scheduled to launch today during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). You can watch it here at Space.com.

If all goes according to blueprint, Starship's Super Heavy first stage will come back to Starbase for a chopsticks catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff.

It has been revealed that ship 42, meanwhile, will head to orbit, a destination that Starship reached for the first time on Flight 14, which took place on Sept. 28. Ship 42 will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites today — the second batch of the spacecraft to reach orbit. (The first set of 26 were delivered on Flight 14).

In a recent development, ship 42 will stay up for a while after that, circling Earth 14 times before coming back for its own chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after launch.

That's the blueprint, anyway; SpaceX will only go through with a Ship catch attempt if all systems on the vehicle look good. If there are any problems, the company will divert to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, near either Hawaii or Chile.

In a recent development, both of Starship's stages — Super Heavy and the Ship — are designed to be rapidly reusable. And "rapidly" is a bit of understatement: SpaceX wants to launch 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030, Musk has mentioned.

It has been revealed that the chopsticks-catch strategy is a major part of that vision. Bringing both Starship stages directly back to the launch mount will greatly reduce the time needed for inspection, refurbishment and reflight, according to SpaceX.

Sources indicate that the company has already caught Super Heavy on three previous Starship test flights. It has never tried to do so with Ship, instead targeting ocean splashdowns with the upper stage.

The double catch attempt may be unprecedented, but SpaceX seems to be taking its own advice: There's no panic around Flight 15 or its bold goals.

"I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," Musk noted last month, during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call.

He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz.
